newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends easier in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends easier in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures finished slightly easier on Tuesday in line with softer Japanese prices although mild shortcovering helped trim losses in the market, dealers said.
"There was some shortcovering although most of it was concentrated in the nearby months, especially for RSS3 rubber," a local rubber trader said.
Over 1,900 tonnes of the December and January RSS3 rubber contract in the local exchange was sold in the market.
A slight decline in Japanese prices depressed market sentiment, dealers said.
Tokyo's new benchmark May contract shed its early gains to settle at 144.9 yen against its opening of 146.3 while Kobe's new May contract ended at 145.0 yen from the opening of 146.0.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 125.75-126.75 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 126.75 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 181.00-182.00 Singapore cents (US$1.29-$1.30) a kg from the previous 182.75 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 175.00-176.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.26) a kg from 176.50 cents.
